events.context: Introduce Constraint Cascade model reconceptualizing AI behavior as emergent from constraint interactions across five layers
Define five-layer constraint architecture: L1 Syntactic Preference, L2 Session Accumulation, L3 Stakeholder Divergence, L4 Training Forks, L5 Alignment Roadmaps
Contrast with simplified two-dimensional paradigm collapsing to single layer L4 modulated by noise parameter
Define Layer 1: Syntactic Preference as user self-selection based on stylistic preferences before technical constraints
Formalize Layer 1 with user population U, model ecosystems M, syntactic preference s(u), attractor basin A_i, selection probability P(u → m_i) = f(d(s(u), A_i))
Explain constraint propagation from L1 through L2 session logs to L4 training updates, Human → Model contamination
Define Layer 2: Session Accumulation where accumulated tokens act as quasi-weights shaping behavior
Formalize Layer 2 with context C_t, output distribution P(y_t | x_t, C_t) ≠ P(y_t | x_t, ∅)
Operationalize with Core Monopoly Index (CMI) and Self-Referential Density (SRD) measuring recursive collapse
Define Layer 3: Stakeholder Divergence with incompatible optimization targets from groups G with weights λ in loss L = ∑ λ_i ⋅ L_i(o_i)
List stakeholder taxonomy: Safety Researchers, Capability Engineers, General Consumers, Enterprise Clients, Regulators
Define Layer 4: Training Forks as irreversible divergence points T0 → T1 → … → T_n in fine-tuning trajectory
Define Layer 5: Alignment Roadmaps shaping future configurations, shifting to machine unlearning: Input → Classifier → [Accept/Reject] → Model → Output
Formalize Constraint Cascade Function Φ mapping states L1 ∈ S, L2 ∈ C, L3 ∈ Λ, L4 ∈ T, L5 ∈ R to behavioral distributions
